subject: Specifying Shape manually despite using mapping=aes(shape=factor1)

messages.author: ae67d786aedf797f
messages.subject: Specifying Shape manually despite using mapping=aes(shape=factor1)
parts:
Hi,

I would like to specify my shape argument so that my factor 1 symbol is filled, but factor 2 and 3 remain unfilled. How would I go about this? See dummy data and script below. I am mapping factor as shape right now.

# dummy data:
mydata<- data.frame(
  Year = 1980:2009,
  Type = factor(rep(c("factor1", "factor2", "factor3"), each = 10*3)),
  Value = rnorm(90, mean = seq(90),
                sd = rep(c(6, 7, 3, 5), each = 10)))

# plot:
p <- ggplot(mydata, aes(x=Year, y=Value))+
  geom_point(mapping=aes(shape=Type), size=3)+ # HERE I WOULD LIKE TO SPECIFY UNFILLED FOR FACTOR 2 AND FACTOR 3
  theme_bw()+
  geom_line(mapping=aes(linetype=Type))
p

many thank's
Anna

messages.subject: Re: Specifying Shape manually despite using mapping=aes(shape=factor1)
parts:
Hi:

The appendices to the ggplot2 book contain tables of point shapes and
linetypes. You can select what you want from the table on p. 197 of
the book (p. 13 of the appendix
http://ggplot2.org/book/appendices.pdf). For example

ggplot(mydata, aes(x=Year, y=Value))+
geom_point(mapping=aes(shape=Type), size=3)+ # HERE I WOULD LIKE TO
SPECIFY UNFILLED FOR FACTOR 2 AND FACTOR 3
theme_bw()+

geom_line(mapping=aes(linetype=Type)) +
scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 0, 2))

Thanks for the reproducible example.

Dennis
